facts: The acute supplement $A=180^{\circ}-\theta$ is the reference angle.
In the second quadrant only sine is positive.
An acute angle and an obtuse angle with the same sine are **supplementary** — they add to $180^{\circ}$, for example $\sin 40^{\circ}=\sin 140^{\circ}$.
steps: Attach the second-quadrant sign (sine positive; cosine and tangent negative)
Substitute the exact value if one is required

workedExamples.question_text: Rewrite $\sin 128^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
Rewrite $\cos 112^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}A&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\&=68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

In Q2, the $x$-coordinate is negative, so cosine is negative.

$\begin{aligned}\cos 112^{\circ}&=-\cos 68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Rewrite $\tan 146^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}A&=180^{\circ}-146^{\circ}\\&=34^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

In Q2, sine is positive and cosine is negative. Their ratio, tangent, is negative.

$\begin{aligned}\tan 146^{\circ}&=-\tan 34^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: Rewrite $\cos 140^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
foundation.solution_text:
$140^{\circ}$ is obtuse, so it lies in the second quadrant, where cosine is negative.
$\cos 140^{\circ}=-\cos(180^{\circ}-140^{\circ})$
$=-\cos 40^{\circ}$

$\sin 110^{\circ}=\sin(180^{\circ}-110^{\circ})$
$=\sin 70^{\circ}$
